claims.text: Severe plastic deformation refines FeMnCoCr-based HEAs into a nanostructured grain architecture.
Severe plastic deformation increases grain-boundary density in FeMnCoCr-based HEAs.
Severe plastic deformation induces lattice strain in FeMnCoCr-based HEAs.
Increased grain-boundary density and lattice strain locally modify magnetic exchange interactions.
Perturbed exchange interactions at interfaces reduce the activation barrier for field-driven spin reorientation.
A reduced spin-reorientation barrier enhances the magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
The enhanced low-field magnetocaloric response consists of larger isothermal magnetic entropy change and adiabatic temperature change.
The fine-grained structure promotes rapid heat transfer.
Fine-grain reinforcement maintains or improves mechanical stability.
The severe-plastic-deformation-treated alloy will have lower magnetic hysteresis than the coarse-grained baseline.
The untreated coarse-grained FeMnCoCr-based HEA has a higher onset field for its magnetic transition.
The untreated baseline has greater magnetic hysteresis than the proposed deformation-treated state.
Room-temperature high-pressure torsion under controlled strain rates can produce a homogeneous nanostructure without unwanted phase transformations.
Mild post-deformation annealing can stabilize the microstructure while avoiding grain coarsening.
The proposed mechanism applies only when severe plastic deformation does not trigger phase transformations.
The proposed mechanism should apply across magnetic fields and thermal conditions typical of magnetic-refrigeration operation.
Previous studies in related systems show that grain refinement can influence magnetic exchange interactions.
